\begin{document}
The dot level is filled up to the Fermi level $\mu$ of the lead. At inverse temperature $\beta>0$ its occupation is
\begin{equation}
n_F(\epsilon) = \frac{1}{e^{\beta(\epsilon-\mu)}+1} .
\label{eq:nf}
\end{equation}
Occupations of a level and of its mirror image add up to one,
\begin{equation}
n_F(\epsilon) + n_F(-\epsilon) = 1 .
\label{eq:ph}
\end{equation}
\end{document}
